record.one_liner: Team messaging and collaboration platform with a developer platform (Web API, apps, and an official MCP server).
record.auth_notes: Apps are installed through the v2 OAuth 2.0 flow; bot and user tokens are issued from that install. Not verified: whether a static app-level token from app settings (for Socket Mode-style use) should count as api_key, so left out.
record.access_notes: Developer sandboxes are free but need the Slack Developer Program. Internal apps can be built and installed in a workspace without vendor approval (not fully verified on the fetched pages).
record.api_notes: Web API is HTTP RPC-style methods at slack.com/api/METHOD_FAMILY.method, described by Slack as not strictly REST. Mapped to rest as the closest enum value.
record.blocker_notes: Buildable now for internal testing with self-serve OAuth. Commercial distribution to other workspaces needs Slack Marketplace review and approval.

evidence.quote: Slack apps are installed with a v2 OAuth 2.0 flow.
Sandboxes are Enterprise environments that you can use to build against all of Slack’s features safely and securely at no cost.
While it's not a REST API, those familiar with REST should be at home with its foundations in HTTP.
The Slack MCP server provides AI agents with secure access to your Slack workspace or Enterprise organisation
apps intended for commercial distribution should be submitted and approved for listing in the Slack Marketplace.
